answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, where agents assign scores based on interactions. An agent's score decreases if its behavior creates an echo of malicious activity. As an attacker attempts to create fake identities, their scores are diluted over the horizon of all agents, making it harder to gain traction. To concentrate their influence, an attacker must anchor their fake identities to a trusted jetty, such as a legitimate agent or a secure data source, at significant computational cost.
